title: Animals, Food and Food Chains
seo_title: Primary 2 Basic Science: Animals, Food and Food Chains Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 2 Basic Science: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Animals get food in different ways; food chains show how energy passes from producers (plants) to consumers and decomposers. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 2, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): producers, consumers, decomposers, food chains, food webs, changes in a food web and energy and the Sun. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy flows from the Sun to plants to animals.
key_sub: Producers make food; consumers eat; decomposers break down dead things.
body_html:
How to think about it

A food chain shows who eats whom. The arrows point from the food to the eater.

  • Producers (plants and algae) make their own food using sunlight.
  • Consumers eat other living things: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both.
  • Decomposers (fungi, bacteria, worms) break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil.
  • A food web is many linked food chains. If one population changes, others change too.
Example

Grass → hare → lynx. Which is the producer?

the grass makes its own food

Answer: grass

Example

If the hares disappear, what happens to the lynx?

lynx eat hares

less food

Answer: the lynx population falls

Common mistakes

  • Drawing the arrows backwards (the arrow points to the eater).
  • Thinking decomposers are not important.
  • Thinking a change to one animal affects only that animal.

faq.q: Why do food chains start with a plant?
faq.a: Plants are producers. They capture energy from the Sun and make food, so all the energy in the chain starts with them.

faq.q: What is the difference between a food chain and a food web?
faq.a: A food chain is one path of energy. A food web shows many food chains linked together.
They break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil so new plants can grow.

items.q: Food chain: nettles → aphid → ladybird → blackbird. Which is the top predator?
items.e: The top predator is at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats it.

items.q: In a pond: algae → tadpole → fish → heron. Which is the top consumer?
items.e: The heron is at the end of the chain.

items.q: Food chain: nettles → aphid → ladybird → blackbird. Which is the producer?
items.e: The producer makes its own food using sunlight; it is always first.

items.q: Are bacteria in the soil producers, consumers or decomposers?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: Are phytoplankton producers, consumers or decomposers?
items.e: Producers make their own food from sunlight.

items.q: What happens to a fallen mango tree in a forest over many years?
c: Fungi, bacteria and insects break it down into soil.
items.e: Decomposers recycle the matter.

items.q: What does an arrow in a food chain show?
c: the direction energy moves when one thing is eaten
items.e: The arrow points to the eater.

items.q: Lake food chain: algae → zooplankton → minnow → walleye. What does the minnow eat?
items.e: Follow the arrow into the minnow.

items.q: Meadow food chain: clover → grasshopper → garter snake → red-tailed hawk. Which is a carnivore that is also eaten?
items.e: The snake eats grasshoppers and is eaten by hawks.

items.q: Food chain: pondweed → tadpole → water beetle → heron. Which is the top predator?
items.e: The top predator is at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats it.

items.q: Food chain: lettuce → slug → hedgehog → mongoose. Which is the producer?
items.e: The producer makes its own food using sunlight; it is always first.

items.q: Is a mushroom a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: Seagrass grows in shallow sea water. What is its role?
c: a producer that feeds dugongs and turtles
items.e: Seagrass makes food from sunlight.

items.q: Food chain: phytoplankton → krill → whale. Which is the producer?
items.e: The producer makes its own food using sunlight; it is always first.

items.q: What would happen if there were no decomposers?
c: Dead plants and animals would pile up and soil would lose nutrients.
items.e: Decomposers recycle nutrients.

items.q: Food chain: grass → rabbit → fox. Which is the first consumer (it eats the producer)?
items.e: It eats the plant at the start of the chain.

items.q: Is mould on bread a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: Food chain: lettuce → slug → hedgehog → mongoose. Which is the first consumer (it eats the producer)?
items.e: It eats the plant at the start of the chain.

items.q: Which living thing is a decomposer?
items.e: Fungi break down dead things.

items.q: Food chain: pondweed → tadpole → water beetle → heron. Which is the first consumer (it eats the producer)?
items.e: It eats the plant at the start of the chain.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: field vole, grain, kestrel?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a prey?
c: a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things
a living thing that is hunted and eaten by other animals
a living thing that eats only animals
a living thing that hunts and eats other animals
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: This is a coral reef food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: seaweed → parrotfish → reef shark.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
c: heron → frog → dragonfly nymph → mosquito larva → algae
algae → mosquito larva → snail → frog → heron
algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly nymph → frog → heron
heron → algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly nymph → frog
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly nymph → frog → heron.

items.q: Look at the meadow food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk.

items.q: Which is a scavenger that eats dead animals?
items.e: Scavengers clean up dead animals.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: mongoose, hedgehog, lettuce, slug?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: krill, phytoplankton, whale?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a consumer?
c: a living thing that makes its own food using energy from sunlight
a living thing that eats only animals
a living thing that eats only plants
a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: This is a coral reef food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: seaweed → parrotfish → shark.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that makes its own food using energy from sunlight?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a carnivore?
c: a living thing that is hunted and eaten by other animals
a living thing that hunts and eats other animals
a living thing that eats only animals
a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a producer?
c: a living thing that makes its own food using energy from sunlight
a living thing that is hunted and eaten by other animals
a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things
a living thing that eats only plants
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: aphid, blackbird, ladybird, nettles?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: fox, grass, rabbit?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: cat, dandelion, snail, song thrush?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that is hunted and eaten by other animals?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: What is a food web?
c: many food chains that are linked together
items.e: Most animals eat more than one thing.

items.q: Use the pond food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
c: algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly nymph → frog → heron
heron → algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly nymph → frog
algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly nymph → snail → heron
heron → frog → dragonfly nymph → mosquito larva → algae
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly nymph → frog → heron.

items.q: Use the pond food web. In this web, the snail's food is: algae, pondweed. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only plants (producers).

items.q: Look at the ocean food web. Which animal eats the seal?
items.e: An arrow goes from the seal to the orca.

items.q: This is a mangrove swamp food web. Which animal eats the crab?
items.e: An arrow goes from the crab to the kingfisher.

items.q: This is a meadow food web. What does the grasshopper eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the grass to the grasshopper, so the grasshopper eats grass.

items.q: Use the mangrove swamp food web. What does the snail eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the algae to the snail, so the snail eats algae.

items.q: Pond food web: algae and duckweed are eaten by tadpoles and snails. Fish eat tadpoles. Herons eat fish and frogs. Which living things are producers?
items.e: Producers are the plants and algae.

items.q: Look at the meadow food web. How many kinds of food does the mouse eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the mouse: wildflowers, grasshopper.

items.q: Bacteria in the soil break down a dead tree. What role do they play?
items.e: Bacteria recycle nutrients.

items.q: Earthworms eat dead leaves. What role do they play?
items.e: Worms help recycle nutrients.

items.q: Look at the meadow food web. Which animal eats the wildflowers?
items.e: An arrow goes from the wildflowers to the rabbit.

items.q: This is a mangrove swamp food web. Which animal eats the mangrove tree?
items.e: An arrow goes from the mangrove tree to the crab.

items.q: Use the mangrove swamp food web. In this web, the crab's food is: mangrove tree, algae. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only plants (producers).

items.q: Use the coral reef food web. What does the zooplankton eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the phytoplankton to the zooplankton, so the zooplankton eats phytoplankton.

items.q: Look at the mangrove swamp food web. In this web, the heron's food is: mudskipper. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only animals.

items.q: This is a pond food web. How many kinds of food does the heron eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the heron: frog, guppy.

items.q: Use the coral reef food web. What does the green turtle eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the seaweed to the green turtle, so the green turtle eats seaweed.

items.q: Look at the ocean food web. How many kinds of food does the sea urchin eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the sea urchin: seaweed.

items.q: Look at the coral reef food web. In this web, the green turtle's food is: seaweed. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only plants (producers).

items.q: Look at the coral reef food web. Which animal eats the zooplankton?
items.e: An arrow goes from the zooplankton to the small fish.

items.q: Use the meadow food web. What does the grasshopper eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the grass to the grasshopper, so the grasshopper eats grass.

items.q: Ada observes that ants protect acacia trees and live in their thorns. What kind of interaction is this?
items.e: In mutualism, both benefit.

items.q: Use the pond food web. A disease kills most of the mosquito larvae. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The dragonfly nymph eats only mosquito larvae. Without them, the dragonfly nymph has little food.

items.q: Look at the ocean food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: phytoplankton → krill → humpback whale.

items.q: Cacti survive in deserts where it rarely rains. Which physical factor is most important here?
items.e: Physical factors in the environment affect which organisms can survive.

items.q: Food chain: nettles → aphid → ladybird → blackbird. If all the blackbirds were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be more ladybirds.
There would probably be fewer ladybirds.
items.e: With no blackbirds eating them, more ladybirds survive.

items.q: Hadiza observes that a tick sucks blood from a dog. What kind of interaction is this?
items.e: In parasitism, one benefits and the other is harmed.

items.q: Food chain: algae → mayfly larva → trout → otter. If all the otters were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer trout.
There would probably be more trout.
items.e: With no otters eating them, more trout survive.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that hunts and eats other animals?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Use the coral reef food web. A disease kills most of the zooplankton. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The small fish eats only zooplankton. Without them, the small fish has little food.

items.q: Hauwa observes that weeds and corn take the same water. What kind of interaction is this?
items.e: In competition, organisms need the same limited resource.

items.q: Nonso observes that fungi on plant roots get sugar and help roots take in water. What kind of interaction is this?
items.e: In mutualism, both benefit.

items.q: Nonso needs an example of predation (one organism hunts and eats another). Which is the best example?
c: a hermit crab lives in an empty snail shell
a tapeworm lives in an animal's intestine
clownfish live in sea anemones and help keep them clean
a hawk dives for a rabbit
items.e: That is predation.

items.q: Mangrove trees grow in salty, waterlogged mud with little oxygen. Which physical factor is most important here?
items.e: Physical factors in the environment affect which organisms can survive.

items.q: Zainab needs an example of mutualism (both benefit). Which is the best example?
c: a tick sucks blood from a dog
ants protect acacia trees and live in their thorns
barnacles ride on a whale without hurting it
a bird builds a nest in a tree
items.e: That is mutualism.

items.q: Use the mangrove swamp food web. Most of the mudskippers are removed from the mangrove swamp. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the mudskipper eats snails. With fewer predators, more snails survive.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: algae, mayfly larva, otter, trout?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Seedlings grow towards a window. Which physical factor is most important here?
items.e: Physical factors in the environment affect which organisms can survive.

items.q: Food chain: seaweed → periwinkle → crab → herring gull. If the number of seaweed fell, what would most likely happen to the periwinkles?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: What is succession?
c: the life cycle of a frog
the gradual change in the species in an ecosystem over time
items.e: A field can slowly become a forest.

items.q: Look at the coral reef food web. A disease kills most of the small fish. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The coral trout eats only small fish. Without them, the coral trout has little food.

items.q: What is a top predator?
c: an animal at the end of a food chain that nothing in the chain eats
the first living thing in a chain
items.e: Such as an owl or a fox.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. The energy in the frog's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the frog.

items.q: What is a consumer?
c: an organism that gets energy by eating other organisms
a plant that makes its own food
items.e: Animals are consumers. They cannot make their own food.

items.q: Which change would affect the most organisms in a food web?
items.e: Every food chain begins with producers, so all consumers depend on them.

items.q: A herbivore eats
items.e: Rabbits and antelope are herbivores.

items.q: Where does the energy in almost every food chain come from first?
items.e: Plants capture sunlight.

items.q: What do we call an animal that hunts and eats other animals?
items.e: The animal that is eaten is the prey. The hunter is the predator.

items.q: Which organisms break down dead plants and animals?
c: decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria
items.e: Decomposers return matter from dead organisms to the soil.

items.q: Sea otters eat sea urchins, and sea urchins eat kelp. What happens to the kelp if the sea otters disappear?
c: It decreases, because more sea urchins eat it.
items.e: Fewer otters means more urchins, and more urchins eat more kelp.

items.q: A graph shows that when the number of snakes in a garden fell, the number of mynahs rose. What is the best explanation?
c: Fewer mynahs were eaten by snakes.
items.e: Fewer predators means more prey survive.

items.q: Look at the ocean food web. The energy in the humpback whale's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the humpback whale.

items.q: This is a mangrove swamp food web. The energy in the heron's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the heron.

items.q: Use the pond food web. The energy in the dragonfly nymph's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the dragonfly nymph.

items.q: Why does a food chain always start with a plant (or other producer)?
c: Producers make their own food from sunlight.
items.e: Producers come first.

items.q: What does a food chain show?
c: what eats what, and how energy passes from one living thing to another
items.e: Arrows show energy flow.

items.q: The number of mosquitoes in a pond fell after guppies were added. Why?
c: Guppies eat adult mosquitoes in the air.
items.e: Guppies are used to control mosquito breeding.

items.q: What is a food web?
c: a web made by a spider
many food chains in one ecosystem that connect
items.e: A food web shows how many food chains overlap, because most animals eat more than one thing.

items.q: What is a predator?
c: an animal that eats only plants
an animal that hunts other animals for food
items.e: Foxes, owls and hawks.

items.q: In a food chain, what does an arrow show?
c: the direction food energy and matter move, from the food to the eater
that the first organism eats the second
items.e: An arrow from grass to rabbit means the rabbit eats the grass; matter and energy move to the rabbit.

items.q: This is a pond food web. The energy in the heron's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the heron.
